title: 2004 HMMT February Algebra Problem 8
statement: Let \(x\) be a real number such that \(x^{3}+4 x=8\). Determine the value of \(x^{7}+64 x^{2}\).

solutions.text:
128

For any integer \(n \geq 0\), the given implies \(x^{n+3}=-4 x^{n+1}+8 x^{n}\), so we can rewrite any such power of \(x\) in terms of lower powers. Carrying out this process iteratively gives

\[\begin{aligned}
x^{7} & =-4 x^{5}+8 x^{4} \\
& =8 x^{4}+16 x^{3}-32 x^{2} \\
& =16 x^{3}-64 x^{2}+64 x \\
& =-64 x^{2}+128 .
\end{aligned}\]

Thus, our answer is 128 .
